4 SAFETY FACTOR The ratio between the maximum discharge capacity of a steam trap and the condensate load it is expected to handle is the safety factor. The safety factor is influenced by ,tbo following; a) Operational characteristics of the trap; b) Accuracy of the estimated or calculated condensate load; and e) Pressure conditions at the inlet and outlet of the trap. 4.1 If the condensate load and pressstre oondition .can be accurately determined, the safety factor can be held to a minimum, thus avoiding oversizing of the trap. Oversized traps, especially and balanced inverted bucket, thermodynamic pressuriz thermostatic types, not only cost more initially but also operate less efficiently creating abnormal back pressures and reduced operating lifetimes.

Where the condensate temp is below the saturation steam temp corresponding to a pressure equal to (a) + (b) above that is where no flashing takes place, then it is adequate to assess friction drop by any of the usual formulae for water flow in pipe.

b) Where condensate temp is such that flashing will occur as the condensate enters the lower pressure zone in the condensate main, the normal water flow formdae are inadequate because both steam and water are passing in the line. In order to assess the friction loss in condensate lines where flashing occurs, it is recommended that any of the usual formulae for water flow in pipes be used, but the quantity of condcnsate flowing be assumed to be equal to W, -+ F, whexe F i; a tlashing factor whose
